title: Quarters and an end-of-quarter adjuster

blocks.text: `LocalDate` has no `getQuarter()`, and calendar logic such as "the last day of the quarter" is best written as a `TemporalAdjuster`, applied with `with(...)` just like the built-in ones in `TemporalAdjusters`. Quarter 1 is January to March, quarter 2 April to June, quarter 3 July to September and quarter 4 October to December.

items: `static int quarterOf(LocalDate date)` returns the quarter (1 to 4) of `date`.

`static TemporalAdjuster endOfQuarter()` returns an adjuster that moves a date to the last day of its quarter. It must work on any temporal that has a date, such as a `LocalDateTime`, and leave everything else about it (such as the time of day) as it was.

cases.says: Mid-quarter dates report their quarter, and the adjuster moves them to the quarter's last day.
March is in the first quarter, September in the third and December in the fourth.
The first and fourth quarters end on March 31 and December 31.
Applied to a LocalDateTime, the adjuster gives a LocalDateTime at the same time of day.

concepts: A TemporalAdjuster, built in or custom, is applied with with() and can work on any temporal that has the fields it needs.
The quarter of a date comes from IsoFields.QUARTER_OF_YEAR or (month - 1) / 3 + 1.
